"The Name of the Wind" by Patrick Rothfuss is a three (I think, it's ongoing) part series which stars a wizard in a world where magic is a rare and powerful thing. While there is magic, gods and demons of a sort, its exceedingly rare, and those actually powerful enough to wield the arcane are usually driven insane by the vast energies no one can fully control.

Kvothe narrates his own tragedy, found by a chronicler who wants to record it. Already his name is spoken as a legend, and he wants to set the record straight.

As a character Kvothe is at times too perfect, but Rothfuss deftly avoids letting him become a Mary Sue. weaving humanity and humility into his protagonist. Consequently, you feel embarrased along with him when he does something achingly stupid and you feel sorry for him as he relates his story, for he's clearly a broken man.

I'm completely in love with the series so far, and can't wait for the next (last?) book which should be out in 2016.
